stories.title: Reverse-engineering is cheap now
stories.summary:
↳ WHAT'S NEW
Simon Willison's observation: coding agents have collapsed the cost of reverse-engineering home devices to the point where it's now a routine weekend project rather than a specialist undertaking.

↳ THE REAL STORY
The ROI calculation on reverse-engineering has flipped. Before agents, the work was technically feasible but economically irrational for most people — hours of effort to automate one device, with the knowledge rarely transferable. Now the same task takes a fraction of the time, and the agent handles the tedious parts: sniffing traffic, writing the integration code, iterating on failures. The practical result is that any developer with a home device and mild curiosity can now produce working automations that previously required either deep expertise or a dedicated weekend. This isn't about capability — it's about friction. When friction drops far enough, behavior changes at scale.
stories.considerations: The catch nobody is talking about: the same dynamic applies to less benign targets. If reverse-engineering a smart thermostat is now a casual afternoon task, so is probing the protocol of a neighbor's garage door opener or a cheap IoT lock. The security community has long operated on the implicit assumption that reverse-engineering effort acts as a natural barrier. That barrier is eroding fast, and most consumer device manufacturers are not updating their threat models to match.

stories.title: Kimi K3 Model Release
stories.summary:
↳ WHAT'S NEW
Kimi K3 is Moonshot AI's latest model release, details of which remain sparse beyond the announcement itself.

↳ THE REAL STORY
With only a name and a vague framing about "global implications on the AI ecosystem," there is nothing concrete to evaluate here — no benchmark numbers, no context window specs, no API pricing, no architecture details. Moonshot AI has a track record with Kimi (their long-context model line gained attention for 128K+ context handling), but this excerpt gives developers nothing actionable to work with today.
stories.considerations:
↳ WORTH WATCHING
The source material is essentially empty — a title and a marketing phrase. Before treating K3 as signal worth tracking, wait for independent evals, actual API access, or at minimum a technical report. "Global implications" language with zero supporting data is a red flag, not a teaser. Check Moonshot's official channels and community benchmarks before allocating any engineering attention to this one.

stories.title: Who's Afraid of Chinese Models?
stories.summary:
↳ WHAT'S NEW
Stratechery's Ben Thompson proposes a policy framework aimed at letting US open models compete more directly with Chinese counterparts — while calling out the inconsistency of labs prohibiting distillation from their models when those same models were trained on unlicensed data.

↳ THE REAL STORY
The excerpt cuts off before Thompson's actual proposal is visible, so the specific mechanism isn't available here. The framing, though, is pointed: US labs are trying to have it both ways — training on scraped data, then locking down outputs to prevent others from doing the same. If Thompson's proposal involves loosening distillation restrictions on frontier US models, the practical effect would be that open-source developers could legally build smaller, deployable models from GPT or Claude outputs — closing the gap with DeepSeek and Qwen without needing the same compute budget.
stories.considerations: The core tension Thompson is poking at is real: Chinese open models like Qwen and DeepSeek have no such distillation restrictions, which gives the open-source ecosystem outside the US a structural advantage. But the missing blockquote is doing a lot of work here — without seeing the actual proposal, it's impossible to evaluate whether it's a serious policy pitch or a thought experiment. Worth finding the full piece before treating this as a concrete recommendation.

stories.title: [AINews] not much happened today
stories.summary:
↳ WHAT'S NEW
No significant AI releases, model drops, or API changes landed today worth covering.

↳ THE REAL STORY
Some days the pipeline is dry. Nothing shipped that materially changes how you build, what you pay, or what's possible. Latent Space called it — a quiet day.
stories.considerations:
↳ WORTH WATCHING
Quiet days are worth noting in their own right. The cadence of AI releases has been so relentless that a day with nothing is almost anomalous. Either labs are heads-down before a larger drop, or the announcement cycle is finally normalizing. Either way, it's a reasonable moment to catch up on what shipped last week rather than chase today's noise.
